name: Cable Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
summary: A unilateral vertical pulling exercise performed on a high cable pulley to target the latissimus dorsi and elbow flexors while challenging core stability.

setup: Attach a single D-handle to the high pulley of a lat pulldown or cable station.
Adjust the thigh pads so your legs are firmly secured beneath them when seated.
Grasp the handle with one hand using a neutral grip, sit down with feet flat on the floor, and allow your working arm to extend fully overhead.
steps: Initiate the movement by depressing your shoulder blade and driving your elbow down toward your hip.
Pull the handle down smoothly along the side of your body until your elbow reaches your ribcage and your lat is fully contracted.
Pause briefly at the bottom without twisting or leaning your torso.
Control the handle back up to the starting position, allowing the scapula to elevate and the lat to stretch fully under control.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the handle down, and inhale as you return the weight to the overhead position.
cues: Drive your elbow down into your back pocket.
Keep your chest proud and your ribs locked down.
Do not rotate your torso to heave the weight.

common_faults.fault: Rotating the torso toward the working side to complete the repetition.
common_faults.correction: Brace the core and keep the shoulders square throughout the entire set.

common_faults.fault: Leading the pull with the forearm and bicep instead of the back.
common_faults.correction: Depress the scapula first and focus on driving the elbow down rather than pulling with the hand.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the range of motion short at the top.
common_faults.correction: Allow the arm to reach full extension and the shoulder blade to elevate for a complete stretch on the lat.

precautions: Ensure the thigh pad holds your lower body securely to prevent being lifted out of the seat.
